dictionary.Data Depth: How much the file actually contains. Many RWR entries carry only a type and a name - those rows are genuinely empty, not a parse failure.
dictionary.Name Matches File: No means the in-file name disagrees with the file it lives in. us_an_apg_73 is labelled 'AN/APG-65'. Check before quoting.
dictionary.Search Range @ Ref RCS (m): The raw stated range, from the longest-ranged search transceiver.
dictionary.Reference RCS (m2): The target size that raw range was quoted against. Without this the range is meaningless.
dictionary.Detects 1 m2 Fighter At (km): DERIVED. Raw range scaled to a 1 m2 target by the fourth-root RCS relation. Standard radar physics, not a stated value.
dictionary.Detects 5 m2 Aircraft At (km): DERIVED, same relation, against a 5 m2 target.
dictionary.Track Range @ Ref RCS (km): Longest range among transceivers used for tracking, at their own reference RCS.
dictionary.Reach Rating: Percentile against other radars within +/- 1.0 BR on normalised 1 m2 range. Withheld below 15 peers.
dictionary.Look-Down Capable: From the groundClutter flag on the signal sets. Yes means flying low will not hide you.
dictionary.Notch Window (m/s): mainBeamNotchWidth - the closure band you must stay inside to fall out of the Doppler gate. The tightest one across the set's modes.
dictionary.How To Beat It: Plain-English version of the notch and clutter columns.
dictionary.Missile Guidance Channels: launchedMissilesPredictedPositionsMax - how many missiles it can support at once.
dictionary.Has ACM / Dogfight Modes: An ACM or helmet-cued pattern set exists.
dictionary.Has Illuminator: A separate illumination transmitter is present - needed for semi-active missiles.
dictionary.Widest Scan Azimuth (deg): Largest azimuth span across the set's scan patterns.
dictionary.Fastest Revisit (s): DERIVED: scan period x bar count. How long between looks at the same patch of sky.
dictionary.Bands: Engine radar band indices. Matters for whether an RWR can see this set.
dictionary.Scope Ranges (m): Selectable display ranges on the scope.
dictionary.Pattern Sets: Named mode groups: search, tws, acmLock, irstSearch, hmdLock and so on.
dictionary.Mode: Transceiver name inside the file: mprf, hprf, hprfVelocity, search, track, common.
dictionary.Active: 'No - receive only' marks a passive receiver such as an RWR or ESM set.
dictionary.Transmit Power (kW): Transmitter power. Absent on passive receivers.
dictionary.Range @ Ref RCS (m): Detection range at that mode's own reference RCS.
dictionary.Absolute Max Range (m): rangeMax - the hard ceiling regardless of target size.
dictionary.Azimuth Beam Half-Width (deg): antenna.angleHalfSens. Narrower means better resolution and harder to find you.
dictionary.Side Lobe Attenuation (dB): How far down the side lobes sit. Deeper means less chance of a spurious lock.
dictionary.Volume Swept (deg2): DERIVED: azimuth span x elevation span. How much sky the pattern covers.
dictionary.Rejects Ground Clutter: From groundClutter. 'No - clutter limited' means the mode is blind against ground return.
dictionary.Notch Max Elevation (deg): Above this elevation the notch stops working.
dictionary.Range Gate Min (m): Closest range the mode will accept a return from.
dictionary.Unambiguous Range (m): Beyond this, range readings fold and become ambiguous.
dictionary.Angular Accuracy (deg): Bearing error of the track. Drives lock quality for missile handoff.
dictionary.Closure Min (m/s): Lower edge of the Doppler acceptance window.
dictionary.Doppler Gate Width (m/s): Width of the tracking gate in closure rate.
dictionary.Platform Domain: Air or Ground, from the platform's move type.

readme: War Thunder — Sensors: radar, RWR, IRST, laser warning
!! READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING ANY RANGE !!

Every detection range in the game files is quoted against a specific target size. The AN/APG-65 line reads 140 km - but that is against a 3 m2 target. Against a 1 m2 fighter the same set reaches about 106 km.

Normalises every range to two common targets - a 1 m2 fighter and a 5 m2 aircraft - so sets can be compared. Radar range scales with the FOURTH ROOT of target RCS. That relation is standard radar physics, not a value read out of the files. The raw range and its reference RCS are kept alongside so you can check the maths.
These are clean-air figures. Multipath, terrain masking and jamming are modelled by the engine and are not in these numbers.
458 total: 315 radar, 98 radar warning receivers, 22 missile launch warning, 19 laser warning, 3 laser designator.
644 transceiver modes, 2017 scan patterns, 1220 signal sets.
2014 sensor-to-platform links across aircraft, helicopters and ground vehicles.
40 sensors are not referenced by any platform - dev leftovers or not yet released.
THE THREE QUESTIONS THE GUIDE ANSWERS
1. How far does it see me
Detects 1 m2 Fighter At (km) and Detects 5 m2 Aircraft At (km). Median across all radars is 33.4 km against a 1 m2 fighter.
2. Can it see me down low
Look-Down Capable. 'Yes - pulse Doppler' means going low will not hide you. 'No - ground clutter limits it' means it will. Read off the groundClutter flag on each signal set.
Notch Window (m/s), taken from mainBeamNotchWidth, plus a plain-English line in How To Beat It. Fly perpendicular and hold closure inside that window and you fall out of the Doppler gate.
A radar is rated against other radars carried by platforms within +/- 1.0 BR, on normalised 1 m2 range. Long = top quarter of that bracket. Short = bottom quarter.
Unlike armour, the numbers here are stated directly in the files - nothing is missing that would invert a result. So a percentile is safe to publish.
Where a bracket has fewer than 15 peer radars the rating is withheld and says how many peers it found. A percentile over 4 sets is noise.
16 radars quote a range with no RCS attached. Their range cannot be normalised, so they are not ranked.
DATA DEPTH — NOT EVERY SENSOR IS EQUAL

Many RWR and laser-warning entries carry only a type and a name. AN/ALR-56M has no transceiver block at all. Those rows are genuinely empty, not a parsing failure - the Data Depth column says which is which.

130 of 454 sensors carry a name that does not match their file. Some are harmless formatting; at least one is a real copy-paste - us_an_apg_73 is labelled 'AN/APG-65' in its own file. Check this flag before quoting a sensor by name.
GAME values, not real-world values. Radar performance is retuned often.
Search range is taken from the longest-ranged search or scan transceiver. Some sets reach further in velocity-search than in range-while-search; the Radar Modes sheet has every mode separately.
The notch window is per signal set. The guide shows the tightest one, because that is the hardest to exploit. Wider gates on other modes are on the Signal Processing sheet.
Ground radars and aircraft radars share one table. Filter on Platform Domains.
IRST and thermal sights are typed as radar in the files where they share the seeker framework. Check the Bands column.
START HERE. One row per sensor answering the three questions above. Reach and look-down are colour-coded from the attacker's point of view - red is bad news for you.
Every transceiver: band, power, reference RCS, range, beam width, PRF.
Azimuth and elevation span, bars, period, revisit time, stabilisation limits.
Range and Doppler gates, notch width, accuracy, IFF, clutter rejection.
Which platform carries which sensor, with BR. Join table.
Every column and its source key.
Platform ID matches the Vehicle ID and aircraft IDs used in the ground and air workbooks.
